subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Acme Corp
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@acmecorp.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-12T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Acme Corp

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today  really appreciate the context on Acme's inference needs. Below is a short recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you described:
- Unpredictable latency during peaks (black Friday + product launches) causing poor UX and retries.
- Cost volatility from shared-hosted endpoints  hard to forecast monthly spend.
- Data isolation requirements for a subset of models handling PII/regulated content.

Current stack / constraints:
- Core model hosting today: self-managed endpoints on GCP (K80/n1) with custom autoscaling (horizontal)  currently maxing at ~40 TPS for text-gen workloads.
- Batch embedding jobs run on separate infra (AWS)  ~20% of tokens are embedding traffic.
- Security: In-house KMS for keys; SOC2 Type II in progress.

Success criteria you called out:
- Predictable throughput at 200 TPS sustained for product pages with 95th p99 latency < 250ms.
- Strict network/data isolation for regulated models (VPC + dedicated GPUs).
- Predictable unit cost per token (forecastable within +/- 10%).

Why Dedicated capacity could be a fit:
- Reserved GPU pools give predictable throughput and isolation (meets VPC/tenant isolation ask).
- Configurable autoscaling policies + burst capacity to handle spikes without shared noisy neighbors.
- Observability and trace-level latency/cost breakdowns to help forecasting.

Open/clarifying items (please confirm or add):
1) Target baseline: you mentioned 200 TPS sustained  is that peak sustained during launches or a steady-state target?
2) Burst profile: expected one-off peaks today are ~3x baseline for <2 hours  is that consistent?
3) Which models need isolation vs which can stay on shared hosting?
4) Any hard constraints on budget or contract term for reserved capacity?

Next steps I propose:
- I will share a short Dedicated overview + rough cost estimate for 200 TPS baseline + 3x burst profile (attachment).
- Rishi (cc'd) will scope a quick perf runbook and compatibility checklist for your current models (quantization/sequence length).
- Schedule a follow-up: 30-min technical deep-dive next week to validate perf numbers and confirm isolation controls.

Proposed slots: Wed 3/17 9-11am PT or Thu 3/18 1-3pm PT  or pick a time on my calendar: https://calendly.com/aisha-rahman/redwood-dedicated-demo

Attachments: Redwood-Dedicated-Overview.pdf (high-level fit + config options)

Thanks!

--
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0123

Redwood Inference  Fast, predictable LLM inference for production
From: Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@acmecorp.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-03-12T17:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Acme Corp

Thanks Aisha  this is a great summary, appreciate the clarity. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Baseline: when I said 200 TPS I meant steady-state for peak marketing pages during launches (we currently see that for ~6-8 hours on launch day). Our true steady-state (daily average) is closer to 40-60 TPS.
- Burst: yes, our spikes have been up to ~3x for short windows (1-3 hours), historically tied to campaigns.
- Isolation: only 2 models require strict isolation (user_profile_scorer, claims_analyzer)  the rest can remain in shared environments. We'll need KMS-integration + audit logs for those 2 models.
- Budget: we have an initial RFP budget range and procurement will prefer annual committed pricing if SLAs and isolation controls are guaranteed.

I'll upload our estimated token/usage spreadsheet to share with you later today (heads-up: embedding volume is seasonal).

For next week, Thu 3/18 1:30pm PT works for Tom and me  booked on your calendar.

Best,
Sarah
Director of Product, Acme Corp
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-03-13T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Acme Corp

Perfect  thanks for the clarifications, Sarah. Quick notes:

- We'll treat 200 TPS as your campaign peak target for the cost/architecture estimate and size reserved pools to sustain that with autoscaling headroom for 3x bursts.
- Rishi will reach out this afternoon with a short compatibility checklist and one-off perf tests we'd like to run against a sample model (nothing that impacts production; can be run against a dev snapshot).
- Please send the token/usage spreadsheet when you can  that will let us produce a 12-month forecast and committed pricing scenario.

Attaching the Redwood Dedicated overview and a template for usage if helpful. Looking forward to the deep-dive on Thu 3/18 at 1:30pm PT.

--
Aisha
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
